messages.subject: Specifying random-slope models
parts:
I'm trying to understand the difference between two
ways of specifying random-slope models in INLA:

First,

y ~ 1 + f(G,X,model="iid")

and second,

y ~ 1 + X + f(G,X,model="iid")

Am I correct that the mean of the fixed-effect coefficient
on X in the second specification PLUS the corresponding
mean random effect there should (approximately) equal
the corresponding random effect in the first specification?

If not, then what is the difference between the two?

Many thanks!

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Specifying random-slope models
parts:
Let u be the normal iid effect with unknown precision, then the first
model says that

predictor = intercept + X * u

while the second model says that

predictor = intercept + beta * X + X * u

where beta is the regression coefficient for X.
